description: Have runSidecar self-register its own pid at boot so the CLI liveness gate sees a standalone-launched sidecar as alive.

userStories.title: Self-register sidecar pid at boot via writeSidecarPidFn DI seam
userStories.description: As an operator running the coherence-rebuild ritual (nohup cam sidecar ...), I need the standalone sidecar to write its own pid into .claude/.cam-sidecar.pid at boot so that cam plan/next/ship's liveness gate reports the healthy sidecar as running instead of sending me to `cam run` (which would spawn a second orchestrator).
acceptanceCriteria: runSidecar self-registers the sidecar's own pid at boot: a new test at test/supervisor/sidecar-self-pid.test.ts boots runSidecar with an injected immediately-resolving runSidecarLoopFn and cwd set to a fresh temp dir (mkdtempSync + rmSync cleanup), then asserts sidecarAlive(join(tmpCwd, '.claude')) is true afterward. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/sidecar-self-pid.test.ts]

The self-write goes through a new injectable DI seam named writeSidecarPidFn on SidecarOptions, defaulting to writeSidecarPid, consistent with the existing writeSessionStartFn seam. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'writeSidecarPidFn' src/commands/sidecar.ts]
writeSidecarPid is imported into src/commands/sidecar.ts from the sidecar-pid module. [oracle: file-assert grep -q "writeSidecarPid" src/commands/sidecar.ts]
The existing pid-helper suite still passes (no regression to writeSidecarPid/readSidecarPid/sidecarAlive/removeSidecarPidIfExists). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/sidecar-pid.test.ts]

run.ts's existing writeSidecarPid(join(cwd,'.claude'), sidecarProc.pid) call and its removeSidecarPidIfExists cleanup are left untouched. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'writeSidecarPid(join(cwd' src/commands/run.ts]

No new SIGTERM/SIGINT/exit handler, no remove-on-exit, and no pgrep/global process scan are introduced; the refusal message in sidecar-gate is unchanged (explicit NON-GOALS). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

Reviewer confirms: the self-write is placed at boot before the poll loop via the writeSidecarPidFn DI seam (mirroring writeSessionStartFn), writes process.pid into the per-project claudeDir (project-scoped), run.ts's existing write is left as a redundant same-pid write, and all NON-GOALS are respected. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Single-concern root-cause fix (locus A per the spec). Files: src/commands/sidecar.ts (add writeSidecarPidFn to SidecarOptions ~L123/L359 near writeSessionStartFn; import writeSidecarPid from src/supervisor/sidecar-pid.ts; call (options.writeSidecarPidFn ?? writeSidecarPid)(claudeDir, process.pid) adjacent to the writeSessionStartFn call at ~src/commands/sidecar.ts:3383, BEFORE the runContainerEnsureGuard early-return and before the poll loop at loopFn ~L3405). New test: test/supervisor/sidecar-self-pid.test.ts (exact filename, AC1 oracle references it). GOTCHAS: writeSidecarPid is NOT yet imported in sidecar.ts (grep confirms 0). The behavioral test MUST inject options.runSidecarLoopFn to resolve immediately (the loop otherwise never resolves) and set cwd to the temp dir so claudeDir resolves under it; mirror stubbing in test/sidecar-ship-phase.test.ts and temp-dir style in test/supervisor/sidecar-pid.test.ts. Do NOT touch run.ts's writeSidecarPid/removeSidecarPidIfExists. Do NOT add remove-on-exit, any signal handler, or a pgrep global scan. Needs a coherence rebuild after merge (sidecar-executed code). Grep scripts/cam/patterns.md for 'sidecar' before coding.
